newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian PM Gujral storms out of party convention.
newsitem.headline: Indian PM Gujral storms out of party convention.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral stormed out of a convention aimed at strengthening his Janata Dal party on Saturday after angry party workers interrupted his inaugural address.

Gujral was warning his party against the erosion of moral values when delegates interrupted his speech and demanded the prime minister sack three ministers who support a scandal-tainted former party chief.
"If you are really keen on moral values, why don't you drop the three Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) ministers and impose president's rule in Bihar?" the delegates shouted.

The RJD is a breakaway group of the Janata Dal, formed in July by Laloo Prasad Yadav, a powerful low-caste leader who was earlier Janata Dal president and chief minister of the populous eastern state of Bihar.

India's federal police have arrested Yadav in a $280 million embezzlement scandal. Yadav says he is innocent. Three of his supporters are ministers in Gujral's centre-left United Front coalition government, which took office in April.
Parliament has been rocked in recent days by demands that Gujral impose direct federal rule over Bihar, where Yadav was chief minister for seven years until he resigned last week.
Yadav installed his wife Rabri Devi, a housewife, as his successor before he surrendered to police.
His indictment in the multimillion dollar scandal has embarrassed Gujral, who had repeatedly suggested Yadav resign.
"The challenge before us is one of morality, and for the past few months, we have been paying the price for it," Gujral said before the heckling began.
After his party workers began shouting, the scholarly prime minister abruptly cut his speech short, strode away from the podium and left the convention before organisers could stop him.
